name: acorn
description: Visual: A simple, stylized acorn with a cap and a rounded body. Concept: Represents nature, savings, or a small, valuable item. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used in finance apps to represent savings goals, in nature-themed applications, or as a general icon for small items or nuts.

name: address-book
description: Visual: An open book with lines indicating text, resembling a traditional address book or directory. Concept: Signifies contacts, personal information, or a directory. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for contact list management, user profiles, or any feature related to storing and accessing contact information.

name: address-book-tabs
description: Visual: An open book with visible tabs on the side, suggesting organized sections or categories within a directory. Concept: Represents organized contacts, a structured directory, or segmented information. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for applications with multiple contact categories, segmented user data, or a more organized approach to contact management.

name: air-traffic-control
description: Visual: A stylized representation of an air traffic control tower with a radar dish on top. Concept: Symbolizes airport operations, air traffic management, or aviation control. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for airport apps, flight tracking services, or any interface related to air travel logistics and control.

name: airplane
description: Visual: A clean, minimalist icon of an airplane, viewed from the side. Concept: Represents air travel, flights, or transportation by air. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used for flight booking, travel planning, airline apps, or indicating air transit options.

name: airplane-in-flight
description: Visual: An airplane depicted in motion, often with subtle lines indicating flight path or speed. Concept: Signifies an airplane currently in the air, in transit, or en route. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for indicating flight status, active travel segments, or representing the concept of flying within a travel application.

name: airplane-landing
description: Visual: An airplane shown in a descending angle, suggesting the act of landing. Concept: Represents the arrival of a flight or the process of landing at an airport. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for showing flight arrival times, indicating the final stage of a journey, or in airport information systems.

name: airplane-takeoff
description: Visual: An airplane depicted at an ascending angle, indicating departure or takeoff. Concept: Symbolizes the beginning of a flight, departure from an airport, or taking off. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for indicating flight departure times, the start of a travel segment, or in airport interfaces related to departures.

name: airplane-taxiing
description: Visual: A simplified airplane icon is shown from a top-down perspective, with its nose slightly angled to the left and its wings extended horizontally. The wheels are visible beneath the fuselage. Concept: This icon represents an airplane that is on the ground and moving, such as taxiing on a runway or tarmac. It signifies movement within an airport environment before takeoff or after landing. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful in flight tracking applications, airport navigation maps, or booking systems to indicate ground operations, gate assignments, or taxiing status.

name: airplane-tilt
description: Visual: A simplified airplane icon is depicted from a side profile, tilted upwards at the nose, suggesting ascent or flight. The wings are angled upwards, and the tail is visible. Concept: This icon symbolizes an airplane in flight, specifically during takeoff or climbing. It conveys the idea of flying, departure, and upward movement. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for use in travel apps to represent flight departures, flight status indicators (e.g., 'in air'), or in aviation-themed games and simulations.

name: airplay
description: Visual: An icon featuring a screen or monitor shape with three concentric sound waves emanating from its lower-left corner, pointing towards the upper-right. Concept: This icon represents the AirPlay feature, used for wirelessly streaming audio and video content from Apple devices to a television or other display. It signifies casting or screen mirroring. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used in media players, smart TV interfaces, or control panels to initiate or manage wireless screen sharing and content streaming.

name: alarm
description: Visual: A classic alarm clock icon with a circular face, two hands indicating a time, and two small bells on top. Concept: This icon represents an alarm, timer, or clock. It signifies scheduled events, reminders, or the passage of time. UI/UX Use Cases: Applicable in clock apps, calendar applications, productivity tools, or system settings to set alarms, timers, or indicate scheduled events.

name: alien
description: Visual: A stylized representation of an alien head, characterized by a large, bulbous cranium, large almond-shaped eyes, and a small mouth. It has a classic 'grey alien' appearance. Concept: This icon represents an alien or extraterrestrial being, often associated with science fiction, space, or UFOs. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for use in games (especially sci-fi or space-themed), apps related to astronomy, or as a playful icon in user interfaces to denote something unusual or otherworldly.

name: align-bottom
description: Visual: An icon showing three horizontal lines stacked vertically, with the bottom line extending further to the right than the middle and top lines. A vertical line on the left anchors the alignment. Concept: This icon represents the action of aligning objects to the bottom edge of a container or selection. It signifies flushing elements to the lower boundary. UI/UX Use Cases: Found in design software, document editors, or layout tools to align selected items or text blocks to the bottom of their bounding box or a reference point.

name: align-bottom-simple
description: Visual: A simplified icon with three horizontal bars of equal length stacked vertically. A short vertical line on the left indicates the alignment reference. Concept: This icon represents a simplified version of aligning objects to the bottom. It conveys the concept of aligning elements to the lower edge. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful in user interfaces where space is limited, such as mobile apps or toolbars, to provide a clear yet compact option for bottom alignment.

name: align-center-horizontal
description: Visual: Three horizontal lines of equal length are stacked vertically. A vertical line on the left indicates the alignment reference, and the lines are centered horizontally relative to this reference. Concept: This icon symbolizes the action of aligning objects horizontally to the center. It indicates centering elements along a horizontal axis. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used in graphic design software, text editors, or layout tools to center selected items or text blocks horizontally within their container or relative to other elements.

name: align-center-horizontal-simple
description: Visual: Three horizontal lines of varying lengths are centered within a square frame, with the middle line being the longest. Concept: Represents the action of aligning multiple objects or text elements to the horizontal center of a container or page. UI/UX Use Cases: Used in text editors or layout tools to center content horizontally, such as centering a paragraph or an image within its bounding box.

name: align-center-vertical
description: Visual: Three vertical lines of varying lengths are centered within a square frame, with the middle line being the longest. Concept: Represents the action of aligning multiple objects or text elements to the vertical center of a container or page. UI/UX Use Cases: Found in design software or document editors to vertically center elements, like aligning a title in the middle of a header or centering a graphic within a specific section.

name: align-center-vertical-simple
description: Visual: Three vertical lines of equal length are centered within a square frame. Concept: Represents the action of aligning multiple objects or text elements to the vertical center, often implying equal spacing or distribution. UI/UX Use Cases: Applicable in layout tools for precise vertical centering of elements, ensuring they are equidistant from the top and bottom edges of their container.

name: align-left
description: Visual: Multiple vertical lines are aligned to the left edge of a square frame, with varying lengths. Concept: Denotes the alignment of objects or text to the left edge, creating a flush left boundary. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used in word processors and design tools to align text paragraphs, list items, or other elements to the left margin for standard reading flow.

name: align-left-simple
description: Visual: Three vertical lines of equal length are aligned to the left edge of a square frame. Concept: Represents a simple, uniform alignment of elements to the left side. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for setting consistent left alignment for blocks of text, form fields, or UI components where a clean, left-justified appearance is desired.

name: align-right
description: Visual: Multiple vertical lines are aligned to the right edge of a square frame, with varying lengths. Concept: Indicates the alignment of objects or text to the right edge, creating a flush right boundary. UI/UX Use Cases: Used in specific design contexts or languages that read right-to-left, or for stylistic purposes to align elements to the right side of a container.

name: align-right-simple
description: Visual: Three vertical lines of equal length are aligned to the right edge of a square frame. Concept: Represents a simple, uniform alignment of elements to the right side. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for aligning elements to the right margin in layouts, particularly in right-to-left languages or for specific design aesthetics that require right justification.

name: align-top
description: Visual: Multiple horizontal lines are aligned to the top edge of a square frame, with varying lengths. Concept: Represents the action of aligning objects or text to the top edge of a container or selection. UI/UX Use Cases: Employed in graphic design and layout software to align elements flush with the top boundary, ensuring consistent vertical positioning.

name: align-top-simple
description: Visual: A horizontal line is positioned above a series of shorter horizontal lines, indicating alignment to the top. Concept: Represents the action or setting of aligning elements to the top edge of a container or canvas. UI/UX Use Cases: Used in text editors, design tools, or layout managers to set vertical alignment for text blocks, images, or other objects.

name: amazon-logo
description: Visual: The iconic Amazon smile logo, with a curved arrow pointing from 'a' to 'z'. Concept: Represents the Amazon brand, encompassing e-commerce, shopping, and a wide range of products. UI/UX Use Cases: Used to identify the Amazon platform, link to the Amazon store, or indicate integration with Amazon services.

name: ambulance
description: Visual: A stylized side profile of an ambulance vehicle, often with a cross symbol. Concept: Symbolizes emergency medical services, healthcare, and urgent transport for medical needs. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used in maps for locating hospitals or emergency services, in health apps to indicate emergency contacts or services, or in general safety contexts.

name: anchor
description: Visual: A classic anchor with a ring at the top and flukes at the bottom. Concept: Represents stability, security, nautical themes, and a connection to the sea or grounding. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used in maritime applications, travel apps related to boating, or metaphorically to represent a secure connection or a point of stability.

name: anchor-simple
description: Visual: A simplified representation of an anchor, focusing on its essential shape. Concept: Similar to the anchor, it signifies stability, security, and nautical themes, but with a cleaner, more minimalist aesthetic. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for interfaces where a less detailed icon is preferred, such as in navigation bars or settings menus related to maritime features or stability settings.

name: android-logo
description: Visual: The distinct green robot logo of the Android operating system. Concept: Represents the Android mobile operating system, Google, and the broader ecosystem of Android devices and apps. UI/UX Use Cases: Used to identify Android apps, link to the Google Play Store, or indicate compatibility with Android devices.

name: angle
description: Visual: A geometric shape depicting an angle, often formed by two lines meeting at a point, sometimes with an arc indicating the angle measurement. Concept: Represents geometric angles, measurements, degrees, or directional changes. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful in measurement tools, drawing applications, educational software for geometry, or in interfaces where directional or rotational adjustments are made.

name: angular-logo
description: Visual: The distinctive orange 'A' logo of the Angular web framework. Concept: Represents the Angular JavaScript framework, used for building web applications. UI/UX Use Cases: Primarily used in technology and development contexts, such as in documentation, project setup wizards, or lists of supported frameworks for web development.

name: aperture
description: Visual: A stylized representation of a camera aperture with overlapping blades forming a circular opening. Concept: Represents photography, cameras, and lens adjustments. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for buttons or menu items related to camera settings, photo editing, or image quality controls in design or media applications.

name: app-store-logo
description: Visual: A stylized 'A' formed by geometric shapes, resembling the Apple App Store logo. Concept: Represents the Apple App Store, a digital distribution platform for software. UI/UX Use Cases: Use in applications or websites to link to the App Store, or to indicate compatibility with Apple devices like Macintosh, iMac, iPhone, or iPad.

name: app-window
description: Visual: A simple icon depicting a window frame with a title bar and a minimize, maximize, and close button. Concept: Symbolizes a software application window or a general user interface element for programs. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for representing open applications, system settings, or dialog boxes in software and operating system interfaces.

name: apple-logo
description: Visual: A silhouette of an apple with a bite taken out of it. Concept: The iconic logo of Apple Inc., representing its brand and ecosystem. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for branding elements, links to Apple's website, or indicating features specific to Apple products like Macintosh, iMac, iPhone, iPad, macOS, and iOS.

name: apple-podcasts-logo
description: Visual: A stylized representation of a microphone or sound waves within a circle, often associated with Apple's podcast platform. Concept: Represents Apple Podcasts, a platform for listening to and discovering podcasts. UI/UX Use Cases: Use in media applications or websites to link to Apple Podcasts, or to denote podcast-related content on Apple devices.

name: approximate-equals
description: Visual: Two horizontal lines stacked on top of each other, with a third wavy line above them, representing the approximate equals symbol (≈). Concept: Signifies approximation, equivalence, or a close comparison between values. UI/UX Use Cases: Applicable in finance, technology, and development contexts for indicating estimations, ranges, or approximate values in calculations or data displays.

name: archive
description: Visual: An icon resembling a folder or box with an arrow pointing downwards into it, suggesting storage or saving. Concept: Represents archiving, saving, or storing files and data. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used for buttons or actions related to saving documents, downloading files, or accessing archived content in office or system interfaces.

name: armchair
description: Visual: A simple, stylized depiction of an armchair with a seat and backrest. Concept: Represents furniture, specifically a comfortable chair. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for e-commerce sites selling furniture, interior design applications, or any context where seating or home goods are displayed.

name: arrow-arc-left
description: Visual: An arrow begins with a horizontal line pointing left, then curves upwards and to the left, ending with an arrowhead pointing left. Concept: Represents a directional movement that arcs backward and upward. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used for undo actions, returning to a previous state, or indicating a backward navigation path with a curved trajectory.

name: arrow-arc-right
description: Visual: An arrow starts with a horizontal line pointing right, curves upwards and to the right, and finishes with an arrowhead pointing right. Concept: Signifies a directional movement that arcs forward and upward. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for indicating forward progression, next steps in a process, or a forward navigation path with a curved trajectory.

name: arrow-bend-double-up-left
description: Visual: An arrow begins with a horizontal line pointing left, bends sharply upwards, then bends again to the left, ending with an arrowhead pointing up-left. Concept: Represents a complex or multi-stage backward and upward movement, often implying a reply to all. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for 'reply all' functionality in email clients, indicating a return to a previous, higher level in a hierarchical structure, or a complex undo operation.

name: arrow-bend-double-up-right
description: Visual: An arrow starts with a horizontal line pointing right, bends sharply upwards, then bends again to the right, ending with an arrowhead pointing up-right. Concept: Denotes a complex or multi-stage forward and upward movement. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used to indicate advancing to a subsequent, higher level in a process or navigation, or a complex forward action.

name: arrow-bend-down-left
description: Visual: An arrow begins with a horizontal line pointing left, then bends downwards and to the left, ending with an arrowhead pointing down-left. Concept: Represents a directional movement that bends downwards and backward. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for indicating a downward or backward step in a process, or a navigation action that moves to a lower or previous section.

name: arrow-bend-down-right
description: Visual: An arrow starts with a horizontal line pointing right, bends downwards and to the right, and finishes with an arrowhead pointing down-right. Concept: Signifies a directional movement that bends downwards and forward. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used to indicate a downward or forward step in a process, or a navigation action that moves to a lower or subsequent section.

name: arrow-bend-left-down
description: Visual: An arrow begins with a vertical line pointing down, then bends to the left, ending with an arrowhead pointing left-down. Concept: Represents a directional movement that bends leftward after moving downward. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for indicating a transition or step that moves left and down, perhaps in a complex form or workflow.

name: arrow-bend-left-up
description: Visual: An arrow starts with a vertical line pointing up, then bends to the left, ending with an arrowhead pointing left-up. Concept: Denotes a directional movement that bends leftward after moving upward. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used to indicate a transition or step that moves left and up, potentially in a navigation menu or a complex data visualization.

name: arrow-bend-right-down
description: Visual: An arrow starts horizontally to the right, then bends downwards to point diagonally down-right. Concept: Represents a directional movement downwards and to the right, often indicating a continuation or transition. UI/UX Use Cases: Used for navigation in forms, indicating a step down in a process, or showing a flow that moves to a lower-right position on a page.

name: arrow-bend-right-up
description: Visual: An arrow starts horizontally to the right, then bends upwards to point diagonally up-right. Concept: Represents a directional movement upwards and to the right, often indicating a progression or return. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for indicating a step up in a process, a return to a previous state, or a flow that moves to an upper-right position.

name: arrow-bend-up-left
description: Visual: An arrow starts vertically upwards, then bends to the left, pointing diagonally up-left. Concept: Represents a directional movement upwards and to the left, often signifying a reply or a return to a previous point. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for 'reply' buttons in email clients, indicating a return to a previous screen or section, or showing a flow that moves to an upper-left position.

name: arrow-bend-up-right
description: Visual: An arrow starts vertically upwards, then bends to the right, pointing diagonally up-right. Concept: Represents a directional movement upwards and to the right, often signifying forwarding or moving to the next step. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for 'forward' or 'next' actions in wizards or carousels, indicating progression, or showing a flow that moves to an upper-right position.

name: arrow-circle-down
description: Visual: A circular arrow pointing directly downwards. Concept: Represents a clear downward direction or action, often associated with downloading or scrolling down. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used for download buttons, indicating scrolling down to reveal more content, or signifying a 'collapse' action.

name: arrow-circle-down-left
description: Visual: A circular arrow pointing diagonally down-left. Concept: Represents a directional movement downwards and to the left within a circular context. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used for specific navigation actions, indicating a diagonal scroll, or a less common directional input.

name: arrow-circle-down-right
description: Visual: A circular arrow pointing diagonally down-right. Concept: Represents a directional movement downwards and to the right within a circular context. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for indicating a diagonal scroll, a specific navigation path, or a directional action in a circular interface.

name: arrow-circle-left
description: Visual: A circular arrow pointing directly to the left. Concept: Represents a clear leftward direction or action, often associated with going back or moving to a previous item. UI/UX Use Cases: Frequently used for 'back' buttons, navigating to the previous item in a list or carousel, or indicating a leftward scroll.

name: arrow-circle-right
description: Visual: A solid circle with a thick outline, containing an arrowhead pointing to the right. Concept: Represents forward movement, continuation, or proceeding in a direction. UI/UX Use Cases: Used for 'next' buttons in carousels or wizards, 'submit' actions, or indicating a path forward.

name: arrow-circle-up
description: Visual: A solid circle with a thick outline, containing an arrowhead pointing upwards. Concept: Signifies upward movement, increase, or returning to the top. UI/UX Use Cases: Ideal for 'scroll to top' buttons, indicating an increase in value, or navigating to a higher section.

name: arrow-circle-up-left
description: Visual: A solid circle with a thick outline, containing an arrowhead pointing diagonally upwards and to the left. Concept: Denotes movement or direction towards the upper-left quadrant. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used for navigation in complex interfaces, indicating a return or previous step in a diagonal sequence, or in data visualizations.

name: arrow-circle-up-right
description: Visual: A solid circle with a thick outline, containing an arrowhead pointing diagonally upwards and to the right. Concept: Represents movement or direction towards the upper-right quadrant. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for navigation in specific interface layouts, indicating progress in a diagonal direction, or in charting and data representation.

name: arrow-clockwise
description: Visual: A circular arrow that rotates in a clockwise direction, often with an arrowhead at its end. Concept: Symbolizes repetition, refreshing, redo, or a cyclical process. UI/UX Use Cases: Commonly used for refresh buttons, undoing a sequence of actions (redo), or indicating a process that cycles back.

name: arrow-counter-clockwise
description: Visual: A circular arrow that rotates in a counter-clockwise direction, typically ending with an arrowhead. Concept: Represents undoing an action, returning to a previous state, or a reverse cyclical process. UI/UX Use Cases: Primarily used for undo buttons, navigating back through history, or reversing a process.

name: arrow-down
description: Visual: A simple arrowhead pointing directly downwards. Concept: Indicates downward movement, decrease, or proceeding to a lower section. UI/UX Use Cases: Used for 'scroll to bottom' actions, indicating a decrease in value, or navigating to content below the current view.

name: arrow-down-left
description: Visual: A simple arrowhead pointing diagonally downwards and to the left. Concept: Signifies movement or direction towards the lower-left quadrant. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used in interfaces requiring diagonal navigation, indicating a step back or down-left in a process, or in graphical representations.

name: arrow-down-right
description: Visual: A simple arrow pointing diagonally down and to the right. Concept: Represents movement or direction towards the bottom-right quadrant. UI/UX Use Cases: Indicating a download action, navigating to a lower-right section of a page, or signifying a trend moving downwards and rightwards.

name: arrow-elbow-down-right

UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for indicating a multi-step process where the next step is down and to the right, complex routing, or sequential actions.

name: arrow-elbow-left

Concept: Represents a directional change, moving from a starting point, turning left, and then continuing in the original vertical direction. name: arrow-elbow-left-down

Concept: Represents a directional change, moving from a starting point, turning left, and then proceeding downwards. name: arrow-elbow-left-up
description: Visual: An arrow that starts vertically, makes a 90-degree turn leftwards, and then continues upwards. Concept: Represents a directional change, moving from a starting point, turning left, and then proceeding upwards. UI/UX Use Cases: Suitable for indicating a complex navigation path that involves moving left and then up, or a step back in a process with an upward trajectory.

name: arrow-elbow-right
description: Visual: An arrow that starts vertically, makes a 90-degree turn rightwards, and then continues vertically. Concept: Represents a directional change, moving from a starting point, turning right, and then continuing in the original vertical direction. UI/UX Use Cases: Can be used for forward navigation with a detour, indicating a complex sequential process, or routing information.

name: arrow-elbow-right-down
description: Visual: An arrow that starts vertically, makes a 90-degree turn rightwards, and then continues downwards. Concept: Represents a directional change, moving from a starting point, turning right, and then proceeding downwards. UI/UX Use Cases: Useful for indicating a forward or complex step in a process that involves turning right and then moving down, or for complex routing.

name: arrow-elbow-right-up

name: arrow-elbow-up-left

Concept: Represents a directional movement that turns upwards and to the left. name: arrow-elbow-up-right

name: arrow-fat-left

name: chat-circle-slash
